pin_added.question: Is there anything on your real dashboard that tells you the run was complete?
Does the screen keep risk and conviction as two numbers, the way the pipeline does — or does it blend them into one score?

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The run stamp is deliberate: this is the only place the screen could tell you *which* run you are looking at. If your real header doesn't carry it, that is a finding.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Straight off the risk model. The 2.5% alert threshold lives against this number — but the alert reaches you out of band, not through this tile, so a tile showing 1.8% and an alert that already fired are two different channels telling you about the same thing.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Count of Signals that cleared the confidence gate. Drawn with the threshold in the label because the number is meaningless without it — 24 signals at what bar?

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: 3+ insiders, 10 trading days. A conviction signal — it never touched the risk number in the tile to its left.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**I invented this tile.** Nothing you have said implies the dashboard reports on the health of the run that produced it.

I drew it because you have five sources, three of which you don't control, and a parked question about what happens when one is late. If the screen can't say '4/5', then on the morning EDGAR is missing this dashboard looks exactly as confident as every other morning.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**A guess, and the sharpest one on this screen.** You told me risk and conviction are two different numbers computed on two different paths that only meet at the aggregator.

If that is true of the pipeline, a two-axis plot is the honest picture of it: names that are high-conviction and low-risk are the interesting quadrant, and crowding would show up as a cluster.

If the real dashboard shows one blended score instead, then the screen has flattened a distinction the pipeline maintains — which is exactly the kind of drift you said you couldn't locate.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: VaR over recent runs with the alert line drawn on it. Guessed. The value of a line rather than a tile is that it says whether you are drifting toward 2.5% or sitting still — a single number can't.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Daily. Cut from this morning's run. Internal only — by practice, not by policy.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Monday's cut. On a Friday it is four days old, and the card says so — which is the point of putting the cut date on the face of it rather than in the PDF.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
First-of-month cut. August 1st was a Saturday and there is no weekend run — so the monthly cut rode the same Monday run as the weekly one, and both cards show the same date.

Drawn that way on purpose. If 'first of month' means something else when the 1st is a weekend, correct the value.
